question: Is all discoverable Indus evidence indexed with its available metadata, and what would a complete index require?
outcome: Reviewed v6 uses post-trim inputs. 123 rows join to 115 site/provenance entities; 5,652 of 5,680 local faces fall in their label frame. Across 19 CISI 1 ranges, 327 of 493 identifiers match and 166 are absent: 75 in pottery/graffiti sections and 91 in other sections. Complete Pakistan multi-run parsing gives 910/1,040 matching keys; north IM77 total is corrected to 117. Museum confirmed lower bound is 68/114, with 46 unresolved. Eight catalogue sections lack rows. Worldwide object recall remains unknown.
challenge: Post-endpoint coordinator title edits made earlier pins stale; inherited IM77 error and first-run-only parsing required source-backed corrections. Mixed classes, provisional physical identities and inaccessible current inventories prevent a global denominator.
remedy: Preserve prior endpoints; record post-trim hashes, parse all runs with the H356/H354 corrigendum, check seven additional museum joins, distinguish structural field absences and pass 53 proposed batch corrections without changing batch rows.
retry_when: Independent review identifies a correction, or current ICIT/full CISI/holding inventories, new registration concordances or original context/rights records become available. Recompute only in a new dated endpoint with the changed input or method recorded.
